pr.title: Register the ready and block tools one at a time, so the hooks typecheck passes against typed tool inputs
pr.head: 7bd2dffbcca943630e9e530083b36accedf2152a

summary: Projector’s ready and block tools let an agent update a request after the person starts it. Claude Code describes each connected tool’s arguments in generated TypeScript declarations. Those declarations require a hook matcher to name one tool, so the shared loop that registers both tools fails to type-check when their inputs are known.

This change registers each tool by its own literal name and moves the shared CLI and panel-update work into report. The ready and blocked results, refusal messages, CLI arguments, and immediate panel updates retain their behavior.

cards.title: Validation and scope
cards.html:
• The configured gate and exact-head CI pass, including 237 hook tests.
  • Isolated schema-derived declarations reproduce the base’s four errors and type-check the reviewed head.
  • The typed declaration test uses copies of the host declarations with inputs generated from the eight tool schemas. It does not recreate a connected interactive Claude Code session.

groups.title: Register each request tool separately
groups.kicker: Literal tool matchers preserve argument types while one helper keeps behavior shared.
intro: A tool-call matcher tells Claude Code which tool a hook handles. With generated MCP input types, a union of the ready and block names does not select a single overload. Separate registrations let the ready callback access its request number and the block callback access both the number and reason.

The report helper turns those inputs into the existing CLI command, handles refusal, replaces the request in panel state, and formats the tool result. Each registration retains its own failure message.

files.note: Splits the ready/block registrations and shares their CLI and panel-update result path.

checks.text: Schema-derived declarations for all eight tools type-check at this head. The same declarations reproduce the base’s union-matcher error and three missing-input-property errors.

Traced the shared helper against the original handlers: CLI arguments, refusal propagation, panel replacement, and result text are preserved. All 237 hook tests pass, including the ready/block panel test.
